topics.title: Passé Composé (Past Tense)
topics.explanation_en: Used for completed past actions. Formed with avoir or être (auxiliary) + past participle. Most verbs use avoir; a fixed group of verbs of movement/state (the 'house of être' verbs) and all pronominal verbs use être.

rules.usage: aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, naître, mourir, rester, retourner, tomber, passer (+ pronominal verbs)
rules.example: Elle est allée au marché. (She went to the market.)

rules.usage: past participle agrees in gender/number with the subject
rules.example: Ils sont partis. / Elles sont parties.

topics.title: Imparfait (Imperfect Tense)
topics.explanation_en: Used for ongoing/habitual past actions, descriptions, and background in a story (contrasts with passé composé for completed events).

rules.usage: nous-form of present tense minus -ons, + imparfait endings
only verb with an irregular stem: ét-

topics.title: Futur Proche (Near Future)
topics.explanation_en: The everyday way to talk about near-future plans, used far more often in speech than the futur simple.

rules.example: Je vais partir demain. (I'm going to leave tomorrow.)

topics.title: Reflexive (Pronominal) Verbs — Present Tense
topics.explanation_en: The subject performs the action on itself; needs a reflexive pronoun matching the subject.

rules.usage: reflexive pronoun placed before the verb

topics.title: Possessive Adjectives
topics.explanation_en: Agree with the gender/number of the noun possessed, not the possessor.

rules.example: mon frère, ma sœur, mes parents
ton livre, ta voiture, tes amis
son chat, sa maison, ses enfants

rules.usage: 'ma' becomes 'mon' before a feminine word starting with a vowel sound
masculine singular before a vowel sound

topics.title: Partitive Articles ("Some/Any")
topics.explanation_en: Used for an unspecified quantity of something, common with food and drink.

rules.usage: after a negation, replaces du/de la/des
rules.example: Je ne mange pas de viande.

topics.title: Comparatives
topics.explanation_en: Comparing two things using an adjective or adverb.

rules.example: Elle est plus grande que moi.
Il est moins rapide que toi.
Ce café est meilleur que l'autre.

topics.title: Numbers 21–100
topics.explanation_en: Compound numbers; note the 'et' before un at 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 71, and the vigesimal (base-20) pattern from 80.
